answer: Lantern Ledger: each identity must publish a signed, timestamped beacon at a fixed summit interval, and peers record its arrival time and path. Duplicates created by one operator inherit correlated beacon timing and routing traces; the ledger flags clusters whose timing variance falls below an independent-actor baseline. An attacker must run each duplicate on separate infrastructure and clock sources, then maintain distinct latency profiles indefinitely, costing recurring hosting and clock-sync overhead per identity, visible as a nebula of correlated traces until separated.
